notes: Usability expansion - car 5, first wave: the console now speaks human language and teaches the two things every new operator gets stuck on, plus skills are filtered by what your machine actually has. Labels: every credential row's primary label is human wording (Telegram bot token, allowed users, access token) with the internal slot name demoted to a hover title - slot names still appear in server 400 details where troubleshooting needs them, never in the label. Onboarding: the Access card now explains the access token in one breath - it is the WEB_TOKEN written at install time, pasted once into the browser to unlock writes, never writable over the API (lockout protection), and re-pasted after any secrets.env edit; the Telegram card gains a collapsible three-step swap guide (@BotFather new token, write it into the Telegram bot token row, restart the chat service) plus how to update the allowed-users list with your numeric id via @userinfobot or @getmyid_bot. Skills filtered by capability: GET /api/skills/remote now computes available plus missing per skill against the live tool registry, credential-slot presence (names and booleans only, values never) and configured channels - unknown requirements count as missing rather than a guess - and the ORCHESTRATION card shows available-of-total with an expandable per-skill gap list. The website directory page adds a requirements chip column and an honest note that a static page cannot read your machine; check the console card for availability. Verification: new tmp/console_onboard_verify.js 33/33 (zero slot-name patterns in visible labels, collapsible swap guide, availability rendering, remote field shape, bilingual), tmp/e2e_skills_remote.py extended 37 to 58/58, tmp/e2e_skills_catalog.py extended 167 to 176/176 with per-chip requirement assertions and a tightened pack threshold.
